Definition: from G575 and G1209; to take fully, i.e. welcome (persons), approve (things):--accept, receive (gladly).
BiblicalUsage: To take fully — to receive gladly, to welcome. They that gladly received the word were baptized in Acts 2:41, three thousand souls in a day; the people gladly received Jesus when He returned in Luke 8:40, for they were all waiting for Him. Jesus received the crowds in Luke 9:11 and healed them, and in Acts 28:30 Paul received all that came to him in his own hired house for two whole years.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe receiving is the first act of faith and the first act of love. The crowd receives the word, the people receive Jesus, Jesus receives the people, and Paul receives all who come — the gospel moves by welcome, and a closed door stops it. I want my own house and heart to receive the way Paul's did.
